title: Replacing Langston Curl in the Cotton Pickers; the 1931 Camden session
summary: Cheatham replaced Langston Curl as Benny Carter replaced Don Redman, and they made the band's last record in a huge Camden studio.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Now did you replace Langston Curl in the Cotton Picker's band?
Yes. I replaced Curl. And Bennie Carter and I went at the same time.
Now Bennie Carter was the leader of the band?
He was the leader, he replaced Don Redman at the same time I replaced Curl.
I see and you made a record with them --
Yes.
-- in -- in
Camden.
Camden in 1931.
Yes.
Which, as it turned out, was the last record --
Uh-huh.
-- they ever made.
Uh-huh.
And what was the studio like in Camden?
Well it was a very large place. It
reminded me somewhat of the old Victor place, here. That's a big, huge place. The studio was a very large room.
Uh-huh.
You could almost put a band in there and not see it. It was just like a big warehouse type -- I think it's still there.
So if you had just been a year or so later, you would never have had a chance to play with the Cotton Pickers?
That's right.
